quotes.text: The trick isn't swapping out tiles or adding a chatbot. The real solution is to treat Viva connections like a system, not just another SharePoint, landing page.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's central thesis on dashboard adoption.

quotes.text: Don't leave governance to the last minute. It's cheaper to get policies right now than to rebuild things at scale after six months of confused access requests.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear, practical warning about planning governance early.

quotes.text: If you want the dashboard to stay relevant, don't drop in every possible feature. Focus the custom web parts on workflows and data people need almost every day.

quotes.text: Where aces really click is when they don't just display a static feed, but become entry points to business processes, opening ticket details, triggering approvals, or linking directly into deeper workflows.

takeaways: Viva Connections dashboards fail when they offer generic links instead of content tied to how each team actually works.
Clean site structure, audience targeting, sound permissions and mobile testing form the foundation before any customization.
SPFx web parts and Adaptive Card Extensions bring live data and external systems into the dashboard, but need careful authentication, performance and error handling.
hook: Many Viva Connections dashboards launch with fanfare and are ignored within weeks. This episode is for intranet owners, Microsoft 365 admins and SPFx developers who want a homepage people actually open. You will learn how to fix the foundation and use SPFx web parts and Adaptive Card Extensions to surface the data teams need every day.
